question: Does the earnings-to-cash gap add predictive value for a material decline in next-year operating cash flow relative to assets?
status: Specification written before the first model run; not an independently registered preregistration
outcome: next annual CFO/end-assets minus current annual CFO/end-assets < -0.02
earnings_feature: accruals_assets = (income - CFO) / end assets; income uses ProfitLoss, then NetIncomeLoss when absent, with tag recorded
models: Training prevalence; standardized logistic controls; standardized logistic controls + accruals; depth-2 decision tree with accruals
model_selection: None. Logistic C=1, balanced weights disabled; tree depth=2, minimum leaf=15, random state=20261009
training_rule: Refit each January 1 using only observations whose outcome filing predates January 1
uncertainty: 2000 paired bootstrap resamples by company and separately by decision year; conditional on fitted predictions
cohort_warning: Purposively selected currently familiar consumer companies, not a historical investable universe; survivorship and selection bias
coverage_adjustment_before_model_run: Direct Liabilities tag absent for several issuers; omit leverage control rather than infer it. Include ProfitLoss with explicit NetIncomeLoss fallback for income coverage. Annual data chosen to avoid quarterly/YTD ambiguity.
